Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

zumir 0.0.0.9000

  • Initial CRAN submission.

  • Bundles MIR, Vladimir Makarov’s JIT compiler (core, code generator, interpreter and its C compiler c2mir), at upstream commit dc2c763, with local patches that make it build cleanly under R’s compilers and remove the undefined behaviour and memory errors its own C test corpus found under the sanitizers. MIR can no longer end the R session or print from it: its exits and messages go to zumir. c2mir reads no header file: C code compiles the same on every machine. On a CPU MIR has no code generator for, and on Windows on ARM, the package installs without it.

  • cfunction() compiles one C function, in memory, with MIR’s own C compiler, and returns an R function that calls it: no Rtools, Xcode tools or gcc needed. Output arguments are copies, so the caller’s vectors are never changed, and no system header is read, so a source compiles the same everywhere. Arguments are checked and passed in C, so a call costs under a microsecond.

  • mir_function() compiles a function from MIR’s textual form, natively or on MIR’s interpreter, and returns an R function that calls it.

  • mir_compile() compiles a numeric R function, in a subset of R, to native code that returns exactly what R returns, warnings and errors included. Where matching R is not cheap it refuses, at compile time or at the call, with a classed error. Compiled loops stop for Ctrl-C and setTimeLimit().

  • Packages can build and compile MIR code through zumir’s C API: put LinkingTo: zumir in DESCRIPTION and include zumir.h. MIR’s errors are reported through the context, never by ending the R session.

  • A critical review before release (#54 to #108) fixed what it found, each with a test:

    • in the vendored MIR: a code generator crash, an interpreter overflow on calls of 95 or more arguments, labels used but never placed, _Bool and unsigned long long conversions, float.h, NULL, character constant types, _Generic, #if’s ?: and bit-field reads;
    • mir_compile() refuses an empty result block and calls with argument counts R refuses, where it gave a value;
    • cfunction() reads its signature after the preprocessor, so a comment or #if 0 can no longer make it write the caller’s vector; it accepts functions of no parameters and refuses factors and dates for pointers;
    • an interpreted function’s first call no longer allocates, so it cannot fail outside zumir’s error handling; the C API turns every misuse it can detect into a status; unloading zumir with a compiled function alive no longer crashes R.

  • zumir_info() reports the vendored MIR and its patches, which tiers run in this session and why the others do not, and the memory MIR contexts hold. zumir_tier() is the default tier: "native", "interp", or "none" where the system refuses writable and executable memory.

Developed by Pedro Baltazar.
